steps.title: Restore empty content without losing discussion or history
preconditions: Run the complete public tracer app -- test services revision-safety command. The original 18 runtime callbacks and 74 HTTP checks are preserved, with stronger repeated-event and historical timestamp equality assertions; the appendix adds 49 requests for 123 total under the original 200-request cap and 90-second process deadline.

Original fixture provisions four synthetic users/sessions and one active team. Original real HTTP mutations leave two live scenes and one tombstone at head six, epoch two, timing one, with a fresh member lease. No new direct fixture writes are added; new thread/message, restores and refused import use public HTTP.

Create one project-level discussion and authored message, independently checking exact metadata and two journal events at sequences seven/eight. Keep all six original journal events exact. The owner, member and viewer remain live and entitled; no permission transition is simulated.

Capture current snapshot, journal, thread and message list using viewer requests between mutations. Those four read requests are dispatched together but no mutation runs concurrently with them. Equality excludes time-sensitive leases except successful restores explicitly require an empty lease list.

Historical pagination uses the three existing small scene identities and limit one. No large page/byte boundary, malformed cursor, private DO tables, process restart, forced storage fault/race, websocket delivery, live provider or native app is claimed. Restoring does not erase retained historical content.
actions: Complete the original journey, capture its exact final snapshot/journal, and create a project-level discussion plus a single authored message through member HTTP routes.
Refuse fresh member and viewer restore requests to sequence six. Verify unchanged nonlease snapshot, complete journal, thread and messages.
As owner, restore sequence six using epoch two. Require one new restore event/receipt, unchanged live/tombstone item versions and exact retained discussion, with no active leases.
Restore sequence zero in epoch three. Require no live items, three exact metadata-only tombstones, false canImport, exact retained discussion and one new restore event.
Submit a valid fresh owner import in epoch four. Require project_not_empty and unchanged public state/history/discussion.

Restore sequence zero again in epoch four. Require one epoch/head/timing increment but identical tombstone versions. Replay all three prior restore requests exactly and require original receipts without another mutation.
Read exact empty sequence-zero history, then sequence-six history in three limit-one ID-cursor pages. Require original live/tombstone data and event metadata despite current empty content.
Confirm current observations remain exact, users/sessions unchanged, R2 empty, zero outbound and 123 total HTTP checks; dispose owned temporary process/state.

expectations.description: Three fresh owner restores each append exactly one snapshotRequired receipt/event and increment head, epoch and timing once. Restoring the current content at sequence six preserves both live item versions and the existing tombstone; restoring sequence zero tombstones only the two live scenes with one version increase each; another empty restore leaves all three tombstone versions fixed. Each resulting current snapshot has no active leases and retains the exact discussion thread/message. This is visible state evidence, not raw change-table equality or a fault/race proof.

Fresh member and viewer restores are exact 403/not_allowed and preserve nonlease snapshot, full journal, thread and message list. After restoring empty, canImport is false and a valid fresh owner import is exact 409/project_not_empty with those observations unchanged. Three exact owner restore retries return their original receipts despite later epochs and leave current public state/history unchanged. Users and sessions remain exact, R2 empty and outbound zero.

After all three restores, sequence zero has the exact empty historical snapshot and null historyEvent. Sequence six still returns the original two live scenes and metadata-only tombstone across exactly three limit-one ID-cursor pages, with expected versions/data, epoch two, timing one, cursor/hasMore boundaries and original event metadata. Current discussion data remains readable through its own routes; historical snapshots deliberately have empty thread/lease projections. All six original events and two new discussion events remain byte-equivalent values in the current journal before the three exact restore events.

mappings.why: Historical lookup reconstructs latest changes at or before the selected sequence and applies the ID cursor. Three limit-one pages recover the exact pre-restore state; private changes rows are not directly read.
Valid sequence/epoch/cursor inputs reach historical page selection and metadata-only tombstone projection. Zero history has no event; malformed input and large-byte cap branches are not newly tested.
Exact one-item pages distinguish cursor/hasMore boundaries, live/deleted projections and stable historical event metadata. The preceding byte-size break is intentionally excluded.

Fresh current-epoch restores target known current or empty history. Unchanged live content and already-deleted items skip version changes; live items absent from empty history become exact versioned tombstones. Invalid epoch/sequence variants remain in the original chapter.

Each fresh restore advances metadata once, clears active public leases and appends an exact snapshotRequired event/receipt while preserving discussion. No raw change-table or lease-token storage inspection.
Current snapshot exposes exact live/tombstone metadata, retained thread and empty active leases after restore. Empty live content remains non-importable because tombstones persist.

A syntactically valid fresh owner import after empty restore reaches the nonempty-item guard, returning project_not_empty without new items/events/discussion changes. Cached import and all size limits are not newly exercised.

Fresh member/viewer restore requests are refused while authorized owner requests succeed. Exact owner retries are intercepted by the route receipt lookup and return original results despite later epochs; inner cached restore branch is not claimed.
